product_question: Should the app include visual breaks?
evidence_summary: Sustained near work and digital-eye-strain symptoms are multifactorial; breaks are low risk and professionally recommended.
implementation: Offer a 20-second visual reset within a 20–30-minute opportunity window.
allowed_copy: A short break from near focus.
prohibited_copy: Prevents eye disease or screen damage.
key_limitations: No unique optimal dose or universal symptom response.
review_trigger: New high-quality visual-break trials or change in intended purpose.

evidence_summary: A small intervention improved subjective symptoms while reminders were used but not objective dry-eye signs; adherence did not persist.
decision: Use as a heuristic, not an authority claim.
implementation: Target about 25 minutes, allow 20–30; say comfortably far rather than exact 20 feet.
allowed_copy: Look comfortably far away for about 20 seconds.
key_limitations: Small symptomatic sample, short duration, no unique-optimum comparison.

evidence_summary: Reduced or incomplete blinking is plausible; small software studies suggest subjective benefit.
decision: Integrate a low-frequency cue into visual breaks.
implementation: Two or three comfortable complete blinks; optional standalone mode only.
prohibited_copy: Incomplete blinking detected or dry eye treated.
key_limitations: Small and heterogeneous evidence; no camera validation.

product_question: Should the app market blue-light protection?
evidence_summary: Cochrane and ophthalmology guidance do not support retinal-damage narratives or meaningful short-term eye-strain benefit from filtering lenses.
implementation: No eye-protection score, lens upsell, or blue-light damage language.
allowed_copy: Adjust brightness or colour for comfort if useful.
prohibited_copy: Protects retina from screen blue light.
key_limitations: Evening light and comfort are distinct mechanisms.
review_trigger: New major evidence or medical intended purpose.

evidence_summary: Practical occupational and ophthalmology guidance supports reducing glare and improving readability.
implementation: Text size, contrast, reflections, comfortable brightness, screen position.
allowed_copy: Try a setting that feels easier to read.

product_question: Can persistent symptoms be managed in-app?
evidence_summary: Persistent symptoms may have refractive, ocular-surface, binocular, or other causes the app cannot assess.
implementation: Help page suggests appropriate eye-care professional.
key_limitations: No triage beyond basic red flags.

product_question: Should sudden vision red flags be surfaced?
evidence_summary: Sudden loss, dark curtain, flashes/floaters, or severe pain can require urgent care.
decision: Include in safety/help and contextual symptom flow.
implementation: Do not show in routine break UI.
allowed_copy: Seek urgent eye care for sudden serious changes.
prohibited_copy: The app can determine retinal detachment.
key_limitations: Localization and emergency wording require review.

evidence_summary: Dry air, airflow, contact lenses, and ocular-surface factors can affect symptoms for some users.
implementation: Ask only if it changes guidance; avoid diagnosis.
allowed_copy: Adjust airflow if it feels relevant.

product_question: Should the app use camera gaze/distance?
evidence_summary: Potential value is outweighed in MVP by privacy, fairness, accuracy, and claims burden.
implementation: No camera permission or posture/gaze completion validation.
prohibited_copy: We monitor your eyes locally for health.

product_question: Can idle time prove a visual break?
evidence_summary: No input may mean reading or video viewing.
implementation: Pause/reset nuisance timing only under transparent thresholds.

product_question: Should prolonged computer-use runs be interrupted?
evidence_summary: Guidelines support moving more and limiting sedentary time.
implementation: Prompt around one hour with flexible window.
allowed_copy: Break up a long computer-use run.
key_limitations: Guidelines do not specify one universal interval.

evidence_summary: Walking generally shows stronger acute metabolic effects than standing alone.
decision: Prefer walking or equivalent active movement.
implementation: Default five-minute walk/wheel/active movement.

evidence_summary: Five-minute doses are common in positive trials; high-frequency trial showed benefit; pragmatic study tested five minutes.
implementation: Five-minute default with two-minute fallback.
allowed_copy: Five minutes is the recommended option.
prohibited_copy: Five minutes is the universal clinical minimum.

evidence_summary: Large short pragmatic study found hourly offered a useful feasibility/effectiveness balance.
implementation: Soft due 50, target 60, latest preferred 70.

product_question: Should five minutes every 30 minutes be offered?
evidence_summary: Strongest tested acute dose in a tiny crossover study and stronger self-reported effects in the pragmatic study.
implementation: Explicit high-burden label and easy downgrade.
key_limitations: Tiny acute trial; self-selected pragmatic arms.

evidence_summary: Broad guidance supports some movement over none, but exact equivalence to five minutes is unproven.
implementation: Record selected duration separately.
allowed_copy: Two minutes is a useful quick break.
prohibited_copy: Two minutes gives the same health benefit.

evidence_summary: Standing reduces sitting but is less active and long-term health outcomes remain uncertain.
implementation: Position-change event does not reset movement unless user also moves.

evidence_summary: Users may type seated or standing and may sit without input.
implementation: Use “estimated active computer use” everywhere.
allowed_copy: 63 minutes of estimated active computer use.
prohibited_copy: You have been sitting for 63 minutes.

evidence_summary: Idle can represent many non-movement states.
implementation: Record likely natural interruption only.

product_question: Do short breaks replace exercise guidelines?
evidence_summary: No; activity-break evidence complements broader aerobic and strengthening guidance.
implementation: Education note in research/help.
allowed_copy: These breaks complement your wider routine.
prohibited_copy: You met exercise guidelines through desk breaks.

product_question: Should recovery break exist after repeated deferral?
evidence_summary: Long uninterrupted work is undesirable, but no exact 90–120-minute physiological threshold is established.
implementation: Offer 5–10 minutes after repeated deferrals; never alarm.
allowed_copy: A longer reset may feel better.
prohibited_copy: Risk emergency: take a break now.

product_question: Should the app auto-control a standing desk or treadmill?
evidence_summary: Automation can create safety risk; active workstation performance depends on task.
implementation: Explicit user command only in future.
allowed_copy: Adjust when it is safe and comfortable.
prohibited_copy: The app will move the desk for your health.

evidence_summary: Meta-analysis shows small benefits for vigor/fatigue.
implementation: Optional subjective usefulness check.
allowed_copy: A short reset may help you feel less fatigued.

evidence_summary: Pooled performance effect was not significant overall.
decision: Do not market productivity gains without direct validation.
implementation: Measure disruption and performance only in studies.
allowed_copy: Designed to fit around focused work.

product_question: Is an exact work-break schedule established?
evidence_summary: Cochrane evidence is very uncertain.
implementation: Use configurable opportunity windows.

evidence_summary: Prompt interventions can change behaviour; timing quality likely matters, but product-specific evidence is limited.
decision: Use transparent adaptive timing and validate.
implementation: Wait for brief low-friction moments within a bounded window.
allowed_copy: Tries to avoid interrupting the worst moments.
prohibited_copy: AI knows your perfect break time.

evidence_summary: No universal ideal posture has been established.
implementation: Promote comfort, support, and variation.
key_limitations: Does not mean every position is suitable for every task.

evidence_summary: Evidence for many office interventions is low/unclear.
implementation: One-time setup flow.

evidence_summary: Occupational guidance supports comfortable height, distance, readability, and glare reduction.
implementation: Centered primary screen, readable text, comfortable height/distance.

evidence_summary: Guidance supports minimizing reach and maintaining comfortable wrist/forearm positions.
implementation: Keep devices close; adjust sensitivity; vary input.

product_question: Should laptop users get setup advice?
evidence_summary: Coupled screen/keyboard creates fit tradeoffs.
implementation: Raised laptop plus external input for long sessions when available.
allowed_copy: Consider external inputs for longer sessions.

evidence_summary: Systematic reviews show possible benefit in symptomatic office workers.
implementation: Low-risk wall push-up/scapular/sit-to-stand options.

product_question: Should aggressive stretching or neck circles be included?
evidence_summary: No need for high-risk/end-range content in a general low-risk app.
implementation: Use gentle comfortable range only.

evidence_summary: Frequent posture policing is not evidence-backed and may annoy.
decision: Use one-time guide and occasional user-chosen check.
implementation: Settings and optional periodic review.

evidence_summary: Reviews/trials show task and motor demands can affect typing/performance.
implementation: Prefer low-precision tasks; explicit safety onboarding.
allowed_copy: Use only for tasks that feel safe.

product_question: Do treadmill desks improve long-term health?
evidence_summary: They increase energy expenditure/reduce sitting, but durable outcomes are uncertain.
implementation: Track user-selected use only.
allowed_copy: An active option for some tasks.

product_question: Is there an ideal sit/stand ratio?
evidence_summary: Guidance and evidence do not establish one universal ratio.
implementation: Gradual comfort-led alternation.
allowed_copy: Change position when it suits the task.

evidence_summary: Standing-only scoring can misrepresent movement and exclude disabled users.
implementation: Equal-status position-change event.

evidence_summary: Meta-analysis suggests modest benefits with heterogeneity.
implementation: 60–90 seconds comfortable breathing; no holds.
prohibited_copy: Treats anxiety or regulates everyone’s nervous system.

evidence_summary: Potential dizziness/discomfort and no need for a low-risk desk app.
implementation: No hyperventilation or long holds.

product_question: Should a bedtime screen curfew be core?
evidence_summary: Adult evidence is nuanced and largely observational.
implementation: User-defined work shutdown and notification reduction.
allowed_copy: Set a wind-down reminder if useful.

product_question: Should colour filters be marketed for sleep?
evidence_summary: Evidence does not support a simple guaranteed fix.
implementation: Comfort setting only.
allowed_copy: Adjust display colour if it feels comfortable.
key_limitations: Light timing and behaviour are complex.

product_question: Should the app support reduced motion?
evidence_summary: Standards and platform guidance require it; motion/light can worsen symptoms for some users.
implementation: Honor system setting; static alternative; no flashing/pulse.

product_question: Can the app claim migraine prevention?
evidence_summary: No.
implementation: Describe comfort/accessibility only.

evidence_summary: Ethical and accessibility requirements; walking-only design excludes users.
implementation: Equal placement and completion semantics.
allowed_copy: Move in a way that works for you.
prohibited_copy: Standing is the only successful break.
key_limitations: Specific movements still need user testing.

product_question: Should every overlay be keyboard/VoiceOver accessible?
evidence_summary: Platform and accessibility standards support operability.
implementation: Escape, focus order, labels, scalable text, no colour-only status.
key_limitations: Must be verified, not merely claimed.

product_question: Should the app prescribe water intake?
evidence_summary: Needs vary and arbitrary quotas are unsupported; excessive intake can harm.
implementation: Optional user-created reminder only.

product_question: Can system volume estimate acoustic dose?
evidence_summary: No; device/output/content differ and safe listening depends on level and duration.
implementation: Optional generic listening break only.
allowed_copy: Take a listening break if you choose.

evidence_summary: General movement can still be unsuitable in pain, dizziness, instability, or unsafe environments.
implementation: Visible skip/alternative and concise footer.

product_question: Should urgent red flags be shown every break?
evidence_summary: Urgent symptoms matter, but routine alarmism harms usability.
implementation: Localize urgent-care wording.
allowed_copy: Seek urgent help for sudden serious symptoms.

product_question: Should core app require an account/cloud?
evidence_summary: No functional need; local-first reduces risk.
implementation: Local storage and export/delete.

evidence_summary: No; only busy/free is needed.
implementation: Discard titles, attendees, notes, locations, links.
allowed_copy: Calendar is used locally for busy times.

evidence_summary: Core works without it; work patterns can be sensitive.
implementation: Coarse local aggregation; no app names/timestamps.
prohibited_copy: We collect usage to personalize health automatically.

evidence_summary: Potential value but sensitive health-adjacent data.
implementation: Controlled fields, no free text, short retention.

product_question: Should camera sensing be added casually?
evidence_summary: Biometric/privacy and validation burden is high.
implementation: DPIA, fairness validation, local processing, explicit consent required.

product_question: What is the launch intended purpose?
evidence_summary: Low-risk healthy-work-habit support is more defensible than disease/condition claims.
implementation: Align website, App Store, UI, support, and features.

product_question: Can symptom interpretation be added under wellness?
evidence_summary: It may change intended purpose and software qualification.
implementation: Keep self-report descriptive only.

evidence_summary: Normal macOS app access is unavailable; companion architecture is required.
implementation: Minimal derived sync; full core parity without Watch.

evidence_summary: Public Focus Filter is user-configured, not universal silent status reading.
implementation: Explain limitations.
allowed_copy: Pause in the Focus you configure.

product_question: Should invasive permissions be required for meeting detection?
evidence_summary: No public universal signal justifies Screen Recording/Accessibility/camera in MVP.
decision: Use Calendar, exclusions, Focus, and manual pause.
implementation: Best-effort context awareness.
allowed_copy: Uses optional context to avoid some interruptions.
prohibited_copy: We always know when you are in a meeting.
review_trigger: New platform API or sensing proposal.
